Whether RLVR outperforms SFT for recovering pruned reasoning models depends on how the model was pruned.
Under diversity-preserving pruning at 20--25\% sparsity, the two paradigms produce near-identical accuracy (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp; max $1.8$\,pp), yet the pruning criterion creates a 4.4$\times$ peak reward gap.
SFT warmup performs the bulk of accuracy recovery (from $<$2\% post-prune to 51--64\% after SFT, i.e., ${\sim}$60\,pp); GRPO exposes structural capacity differences but adds negligible accuracy, a pattern confirmed at 300 steps where CKA-only reward rises yet accuracy remains unchanged (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_extended}).
CKA-only preserves distinct pathways that sustain RL exploration (\S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}); the non-monotonic $\alpha$ dose-response argues against a layer-distribution confound.

\paragraph{GRPO as diagnostic probe.}
The decoupling suggests that GRPO functions as a \emph{diagnostic probe} for pruning quality rather than a recovery enhancer at moderate sparsity: reward trajectories reveal whether the pruned architecture retains sufficient diversity for RL exploration---information invisible to SFT, which converges to similar accuracy at 20--25\% MLP sparsity.
This reframes the practical question from ``which recovery method?'' to ``does the pruned model support RL exploration?''
The decoupling is not absolute: at 15\% sparsity, GRPO amplifies the CKA-guided advantage ($+$1.51\,pp differential), suggesting that at lower sparsity sufficient headroom remains for GRPO to differentiate; the transition boundary warrants future investigation.

\paragraph{Implications.}
For deployment pipelines that include post-pruning RL, diversity-preserving criteria (CKA-only or high-$\alpha$ \rasp{}) should be preferred, as they maintain the exploration pathways that RL requires.
Our findings complement \citet{selfhealing2025}: while they demonstrate RLVR superiority for unstructured magnitude pruning at 96.5\% retention, we show this hierarchy dissolves under diversity-preserving structured MLP pruning at 80\% retention on Qwen2.5-family models---the gap is an artifact of the pruning criterion, not a fundamental property of RL recovery within this scope.
